rows.label: Trigger
cells: The Class T Sunset Time occurs when no Class T common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class T common stock or an amendment to the rights of our Class T common stock that eliminates our Class T common stock, which in each case requires the approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Trust Amendment Threshold may be satisfied as follows if the Trustees are voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 80% of the authorized members of our board of directors and 80% of the Trustees then in office (in each case, rounded up or down to the nearest whole number (any exact 0.5 rounding up)) if our Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action until the third anniversary of the completion of this offering, upon approval by (i) our Class F common stock acting pursuant to the unanimous approval of the Continuing Founders, (ii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of 40% of our outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by outstanding Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock) or at any time, upon approval by (i) the Class F common stock acting by decision of 66 23% of the Continuing Founders (rounded up to the nearest whole number), (ii) 75% of the votes cast by our Class E common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class E common stock), and (iii) a majority of the votes cast by our Class A common stock (subject to a quorum of a majority of outstanding Class A common stock) or if no Class F common stock remains outstanding and the Trustees are not voting in favor of the action, upon approval of 85% of our outstanding Class A common stock. The Class T Sunset Time does not occur automatically upon the lapse of time or the occurrence of specific events. Any action resulting in the occurrence of the Class T Sunset Time requires approval of persons comprising the Trust Amendment Threshold. The Class T Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver.

The Class F Sunset Time occurs on the earlier of (i) the time when no Class F common stock remains outstanding, including due to the redemption of our Class F common stock agreed to by a Supermajority of the Continuing Founders or upon the dissolution of the Founder LLC, and (ii) the completion of the Class F Transition Period. The Class F Transition Period commences when there have been fewer than three Continuing Founders (not including any successor member who is a Non-Qualifying Member as defined in the Founder LLC Agreement) for 90 consecutive calendar days. A Continuing Founder will be removed from the Founder LLC upon the earliest to occur of (i) such Continuing Founders resignation as a member of the Founder LLC (ii) such Continuing Founders death or incapacity (iii) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, such original co-founders ceasing to hold (together with such original co-founders related holders) on any record date for a vote of our stockholders a number of shares of Class A common stock (including shares subject to options, RSUs, and other convertible securities) equal to at least 2% of the shares of Class A common stock held by such original co-founder and their related holders as of the completion of this offering (iv) such Continuing Founders removal for cause, which includes specified competitive activities described in the Founder LLC Agreement (v) with respect to any successor member admitted to the Founder LLC prior to the commencement of the Class F Transition Period, other than a successor member who is a member during the Class F Transition Period, the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering or (vi) with respect to each of our seven original co-founders, the commencement of a leave of absence approved by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, which may not be approved during the Class F Transition Period or if the grant of the leave of absence would itself cause the Class F Transition Period to commence. Removals due to resignation, death, or the occurrence of the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering occur automatically without any determination by any other person. Removals due to incapacity require determination by a qualified physician jointly selected by the affected Continuing Founder and a majority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of physical or mental impairment) or determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders (in the case of wrongful imprisonment, unlawful detention, or captivity or restraint), subject to the affected Continuing Founders right to contest such determination. Removals due to cause require an affirmative determination by a Supermajority of the other Continuing Founders, subject to the affected Continuing Founders right to contest such determination or, in the case of specified categories of cause, to cure the basis for such removal. Removals due to incapacity, cause, or the failure to maintain the minimum ownership threshold require prior written notice from the Founder LLC by action of a majority of the other Continuing Founders. If a Continuing Founder is removed due to death or incapacity during the first ten years following the completion of this offering, a successor member may be admitted to the Founder LLC and will count toward the three Continuing Founders required to avoid triggering the Class F Transition Period until the tenth anniversary of the completion of this offering. The Class F Sunset Time, once triggered, is not subject to extension, delay, or waiver.

rows.label: Changes in Voting Power and Director Election and Removal Rights
cells: Prior to the Class T Sunset Time, the LTBT, as the sole holder of Class T common stock, will generally have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. The share of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, including with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors or as required by law. Following the Class T Sunset Time, if our Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock and Class F common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect all of our directors. Because our Class F common stock is entitled to an aggregate number of votes equal to 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock, the Founder LLC would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors.

Prior to the Class F Sunset Time, our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that equals 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares of capital stock as of the applicable record date and, together with our Class A common stock, voting together as a single class, will elect the directors other than the Class T directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. Immediately after the Class F Sunset Time, if our Class T common stock remains outstanding, the LTBT would continue to have the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who would constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. However, the LTBT would no longer need to comply with the procedures for nomination, removal, or change in the Class T director designated as the Specified Class T Director. In such a case, our Class A common stock would elect and remove the remaining directors and decide all other matters put to a vote of stockholders generally. If neither our Class T common stock nor Class F common stock remains outstanding, our Class A common stock would have the ability to determine the outcome of all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of all directors.
